title: The multitude marvels
summary: After Jesus finishes teaching, he looks around at the multitude and speaks. He perceives that some marvel and wonder what he will do concerning the law of Moses.

explicit_facts.text: Jesus looks around at the multitude after ending his sayings.
Jesus tells the multitude that those who remember and do his sayings will be raised up at the last day.
Jesus perceives that some among the multitude marvel and wonder what he will do concerning the law of Moses.
They do not understand that old things have passed away and all things have become new.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Some listeners appear puzzled or amazed.
unspecified_visual_details: The setting, time of day, clothing, and the multitude's appearance are not stated.

spoken_dialogue.text: Behold, ye have heard the things which I taught before I ascended to my Father;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jesus Christ (at Bountiful)

narration.text: some among them who marveled, and wondered

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict an ascension in this scene; it is mentioned as having occurred earlier.
Do not depict the law of Moses ending yet as a separate visible event.

title: The law is fulfilled
summary: Jesus explains that the law given to Moses is fulfilled in him and has an end.

explicit_facts.text: Jesus tells the listeners not to marvel that old things have passed away and all things have become new.
Jesus says the law given to Moses is fulfilled.
Jesus says he gave the law, covenanted with Israel, and fulfills the law, which therefore has an end in him.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Jesus continues teaching the gathered multitude.
unspecified_visual_details: No visible symbol or physical event representing fulfillment is described.

spoken_dialogue.text: Behold, I say unto you that the law is fulfilled that was given unto Moses.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jesus Christ (at Bountiful)

narration.text: the law in me is fulfilled

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The fulfillment and ending of the law are teachings, not a depicted supernatural event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Moses or a physical law document unless treated as unspecified design rather than a source fact.

title: Prophecies yet to come
summary: Jesus clarifies that he does not destroy the prophets or what has been spoken concerning future things; the covenant is not all fulfilled, while the law of Moses has an end in him.

explicit_facts.text: Jesus says unfulfilled things spoken by the prophets will all be fulfilled in him.
Jesus says he does not destroy what has been spoken concerning things to come.
Jesus says the covenant is not all fulfilled, while the law given to Moses has an end in him.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Jesus continues speaking to the multitude.
unspecified_visual_details: No future events or prophetic visions are shown in these verses.

spoken_dialogue.text: I do not destroy the prophets,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jesus Christ (at Bountiful)

narration.text: the covenant which I have made with my people is not all fulfilled

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The future fulfillment of prophecy is reported as teaching, not shown as a present event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict prophetic visions or future events as happening now.

title: Endure to the end
summary: Jesus calls himself the law and the light, urges the people to endure and keep his commandments, and says the law and prophets testified of him.

explicit_facts.text: Jesus says he is the law and the light, and promises eternal life to those who endure to the end.
Jesus tells the people to keep his commandments and says the law and prophets testified of him.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Jesus addresses the multitude as he teaches.
unspecified_visual_details: The source does not describe visible light or any other physical manifestation.

spoken_dialogue.text: Look unto me, and endure to the end, and ye shall live;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jesus Christ (at Bountiful)

doctrinal_or_story_notes: “The law, and the light” is a teaching and should not be rendered as a supernatural visual effect.
prohibited_inventions: Do not add glowing effects or literalized metaphors.

title: Jesus turns to the twelve
summary: After speaking, Jesus addresses the twelve he has chosen, calling them his disciples and a light to the people, a remnant of Joseph's house. He identifies the land as their inheritance, given by the Father.

explicit_facts.text: After speaking, Jesus addresses the twelve whom he chose.
Jesus calls the twelve his disciples and a light to the people, who are a remnant of the house of Joseph.
Jesus says the land is the twelve's inheritance and the Father has given it to them.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Jesus addresses the twelve as a distinct group among the people.
unspecified_visual_details: The precise appearance and position of the twelve, and the land's visual features, are not stated.

spoken_dialogue.text: Ye are my disciples; and ye are a light unto this people,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jesus Christ (at Bountiful)

narration.text: he said unto those twelve whom he had chosen:

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The twelve are present as Jesus addresses them; the house of Joseph is identified as the people, not as a separate visible group.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the Father as visibly present; no appearance is described.

title: Other sheep
summary: Jesus tells the twelve that he had not been commanded to tell their brethren at Jerusalem about them or the other tribes led away. He was commanded to say that he has other sheep, who will hear his voice and be brought into one fold with one shepherd.

explicit_facts.text: Jesus says the Father had not commanded him to tell their brethren at Jerusalem about the twelve.
Jesus says the Father had not commanded him to tell them about the other tribes of Israel led away out of the land.
Jesus says the Father commanded him to tell them that he has other sheep not of this fold, whom he must bring; they will hear his voice, and there will be one fold and one shepherd.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Jesus speaks to the twelve in their presence.
unspecified_visual_details: The other sheep and the brethren at Jerusalem are spoken of, not shown as present.

spoken_dialogue.text: That other sheep I have which are not of this fold;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jesus Christ (at Bountiful)

narration.text: they shall hear my voice; and there shall be one fold, and one shepherd.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The sheep and fold language is a teaching; do not literalize it as a flock or enclosure.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show the other tribes, Jerusalem brethren, or literal sheep as present.

title: Why they did not understand
summary: Jesus explains that the people in Jerusalem did not understand because of stiffneckedness and unbelief. He tells the twelve that they and the other tribes were separated because of the iniquity of those from whom they were separated.

explicit_facts.text: Jesus says stiffneckedness and unbelief kept the people from understanding his word, and he was commanded to say no more of the Father concerning this matter to them.
Jesus says the twelve were separated from the others because of their iniquity, which is why those others do not know of the twelve.
Jesus says the Father also separated the other tribes from them, and their iniquity is why they do not know of those tribes.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Jesus continues his explanation to the twelve.
unspecified_visual_details: The people in Jerusalem and the other tribes are not described as present.

spoken_dialogue.text: ye were separated from among them because of their iniquity;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jesus Christ (at Bountiful)

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The separation and iniquity are explained in speech, not enacted as a scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not stage past events or groups in Jerusalem as present action.

title: The twelve are the other sheep
summary: Jesus tells the twelve that they are the other sheep he had spoken of. He says they did not understand him, supposing he meant the Gentiles, and did not understand that Gentiles would be converted through their preaching.

explicit_facts.text: Jesus identifies the twelve as the other sheep of whom he spoke, who will hear his voice and be gathered into one fold with one shepherd.
The twelve had supposed Jesus meant the Gentiles and did not understand that Gentiles would be converted through their preaching.

unspecified_visual_details: The Gentiles are mentioned but are not described as present.

spoken_dialogue.text: ye are they of whom I said: Other sheep I have which are not of this fold;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jesus Christ (at Bountiful)

narration.text: they supposed it had been the Gentiles

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Other sheep is figurative teaching, not a literal flock.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show Gentiles hearing or being converted in this scene.

title: They have heard and seen the speaker
summary: The speaker says that others did not understand his words about hearing his voice or his statement that he would not manifest himself to the Gentiles except by the Holy Ghost. He tells those he addresses that they have heard his voice and seen him, and that they are numbered among those the Father gave him.

explicit_facts.text: The speaker says that others did not understand what he said about hearing his voice.
The speaker says the Gentiles should not hear his voice and that he would not manifest himself to them except by the Holy Ghost.
The speaker says those he addresses have heard his voice and seen him, are his sheep, and are numbered among those the Father gave him.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The speaker may be shown addressing listeners who can see him.
unspecified_visual_details: The number and appearance of the listeners are not specified.

spoken_dialogue.text: that the Gentiles should not at any time hear my voice—that I should not manifest myself unto them save it were by the Holy Ghost.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The speaker

spoken_dialogue.text: But behold, ye have both heard my voice, and seen me; and ye are my sheep, and ye are numbered among those whom the Father hath given me.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The speaker

doctrinal_or_story_notes: “My sheep” is figurative language, not an event involving visible animals.
The people described as “they” are not identified in the supplied verses.
prohibited_inventions: Do not identify or count the listeners or the people described as “they.”
Do not depict the Gentiles, the Holy Ghost, or the Father as visibly present.
Do not change “manifest myself” into a claim that the Gentiles would not see the speaker.
